abstract: Trophoblast neoplasm cases at the Lagos University Teaching Hospital in the two-year period, 1980-1981, have been reviewed. An apparent increased incidence of 1 in 184 deliveries for hydatidiform mole and 1 in 299 deliveries for choriocarcinoma has been noted when compared with a previous review. An association of hydatidiform mole with age and parity was observed in this study. Among patients with hydatidiform mole, 27 percent also had pseudotoxemia and in one case this progressed to eclampsia. In the case of choriocarcinoma, increased parity appears to be associated with a higher mortality. The relatively higher mortality of 31 percent from this study could be related to the long duration of symptoms before diagnosis and treatment, and a plea is made to the general medical practitioners for a better referral system, although the need to create an increased awareness of the clinical symptoms of this disease in the community is also very much desirable. A collaborative study of the epidemiology of this disease in Nigeria is advocated.
abstract_ja: ラゴス大学教育病院で1980～1981年の2年間に扱われたトロホブラスト腫瘍の症例を再検討した。前回の検討と比べ、胞状奇胎は184分娩に1例、絨毛癌は299分娩に1例と、見かけ上の発生率の増加が認められた。胞状奇胎では年齢と経産回数との関連が見られた。胞状奇胎の患者の27%に偽子癇前症（pseudotoxemia）がみられ、1例では子癇に進行した。絨毛癌では、経産回数の増加が死亡率の上昇と関連していた。本研究での死亡率は31%と比較的高く、症状出現から診断・治療までの期間が長かったことが原因と考えられる。一般開業医に対しては紹介体制の改善を、また地域社会における本疾患の臨床症状への認識向上を求める。ナイジェリア全体での本疾患の疫学を共同研究で検討することが推奨される。
